lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Welcome back to Daily Standup for September 11th. The biggest story today is Northwind buying Harbor AI for 2.1 billion dollars in cash, its largest acquisition to date.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Right, and the engine is the prize. Harbor's inference stack serves 40 million requests per day, and Northwind says it will fold that into Northwind Cloud over the next year.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Why pay that much for inference? Is demand really outrunning what they already run?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: It looks that way. Harbor employs 240 people, the deal closes in the fourth quarter, and chief executive Dana Whitfield framed it as a capacity bet, not an acqui-hire.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Next, a result from Lausanne that deserves the caveats up front. Walk me through the 512-qubit claim.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: The Lausanne Institute for Photonic Systems built a 512-qubit photonic processor that held coherence for 3.2 milliseconds at room temperature, up from their previous 128-qubit device.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Published in Nature Physics, right? What did independent researchers make of it?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Priya Raman called the error-correction scheme promising but said scaling to thousands of qubits remains unproven. So, genuinely interesting physics, not yet a machine you would buy.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: What about Driftwood? The summary suggests a 45 million dollar Series B led by Meridian Ventures, but going off the writeup, we haven't seen the details on this one.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: That's the whole story so far. Logistics analytics, 45 million dollars, Meridian leading. Have a great rest of your day.
